note: Expectations seeded from seller listings before any tag was read. Measurements are added by tools/iso15693_magic_probe.py; the expected block is never overwritten. Second order recorded 2026-09-08: 9 physical tags across 7 label types, seller-described as a mystery pack. The bag labels use `UID 0-NNB`, which decodes consistently across BOTH orders: `UID` is a claim that the UID is changeable, and `0-NN` is the writable block range, so 0-27B = 28 blocks, 0-63B = 64, 0-55B = 56. Cross-checked against measurement: our 28-block SLI tags, our 64-block TI cards, and the tool's own LRi2K-56 impersonation target all agree. The FIRST order's plain tags were labelled '1024 bit' with NO UID claim and measured non-magic, so the notation distinguishes magic from plain rather than being decoration.

expected.listing_text: SL2S5302; SL2S5402 ICODE SLIX-S UID  [hand-written: pm3]
expected.note: NXP ICODE SLIX-S. IC id 0x02 per the app's decode table; SLIX-S vs SLI-S is uid[3] & 0x10. No block count claimed, so none expected here -- capacity will say.

SL2S5302.note: Hand-marked `pm3` by the seller, who said these are the ones proxmark can write. The unmarked ones he said need a custom application he did not supply -- so on an unmarked tag a negative result from our probe CONFIRMS his annotation and does not refute the UID claim. Physically marked SL2S5302 to tell it from slix-1k-50x28, the other 50x28mm white sticker. BLOCK COUNT UNKNOWN: the label states no range, and neither proxmark nor our app hardcodes SLI-S geometry -- both read it from GET SYSTEM INFO. Measure before assuming, because whether 56/57/62/63 exist decides if a gen1 attempt is destructive.

expected.note: Same silicon expected as white-coin. If the two measure differently that is the interesting result, since the listings claim they are the same part.

black-tag.note: Confirmed gen2 magic on hardware 2026-08-24 -- gen2 UID write took and read back, so the destructive gen1 probe never ran and no data block was touched. Already in proxmark's default CFG state (64x4, IC ref 0x8B), so the gen2 probe was geometry-neutral: geometry_dirty false. Different silicon from the original EM-Marin test card, which advertises 66 against 64.

expected.listing_text: Chip type: I-CODE2, Memory capacity: 1024 bit
expected.note: THE LISTING'S BIT FIGURE IS TOTAL SILICON, NOT USER MEMORY. 1024 bits = 128 bytes = 32 blocks, but an ICODE SLI/SLIX addresses 28 of them as user blocks (28 x 4 = 112 bytes = 896 bits); the remaining 4 blocks are the system/config area. So expect 28, not 32. Reporting 32 would mean the listing quoted USER memory and this is a different part. IC ref 0x01 is the SLI/SLIX family. Expected non-magic.

white-tag-1.note: The probed representative of the three. Classified non-magic on hardware 2026-08-24; the gen1 attempt sent ordinary WRITE BLOCKs at 56/57/62/63, all out of range on a 28-block tag, and block 27 still read its factory 57 5F 4F 4B afterwards -- so no aliasing, and the tag is byte-identical to its baseline.
